headline: Student wings of JCD and Shibir clash at Jagannath University, several injured
summary: The incident occurred when Shibir activists attempted to enter a university programme with placards, leading to a violent confrontation.
details: A clash broke out at Jagannath University (JnU) today between leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir.
The violence erupted around 11:45am as the chairman of the University Grants Commission (UGC) arrived at the central auditorium for a programme.
The conflict started when Shibir activists tried to enter the event carrying placards highlighting various campus issues.
Several people were injured, including JnU Chhatra Shibir president Md Abdul Alim Arif and JCD convener member Yasin Hossain Saif.
Following the clash, JCD activists drove Shibir members off the campus and subsequently staged a sit-in.
Sutrapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Matiur Rahman confirmed that the situation had returned to calm in and around the campus by 1:20pm.
caption:
Student wings of JCD and Shibir clash at Jagannath University, leaving several injured.

A clash broke out at Jagannath University (JnU) today between leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir.

The violence erupted around 11:45am as the chairman of the University Grants Commission (UGC) arrived at the central auditorium for a programme.

The conflict started when Shibir activists tried to enter the event carrying placards highlighting various campus issues.

Several people were injured, including JnU Chhatra Shibir president Md Abdul Alim Arif and JCD convener member Yasin Hossain Saif.

Following the clash, JCD activists drove Shibir members off the campus and subsequently staged a sit-in.

Sutrapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Matiur Rahman confirmed that the situation had returned to calm in and around the campus by 1:20pm.

headline_marked: [[July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum]] to open August 6
headline: July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum to open August 6
summary: The museum will preserve the history of the July uprising, with tickets available online for 50 BDT for adults and 25 BDT for children.
details: The 'July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' is set to open to the public on August 6 to preserve the history of the July uprising.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will formally inaugurate the museum on Wednesday, August 5, at 9:00 AM.
Culture Minister Nitai Rai Chowdhury and Information and Broadcasting Advisor Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman announced the details during a press conference at the Secretariat on Tuesday.
The inauguration ceremony will feature reminiscences from July fighters and members of the families of the martyrs.
A documentary film created about the July mass uprising will also be screened during the event.
Visitors can enter the museum by purchasing tickets online, with a limited number of visitors allowed per day.
Tickets are priced at 50 BDT for adults and 25 BDT for children.
Culture Minister Nitai Rai Chowdhury stated that action will be taken if specific allegations of corruption in the museum's construction are received.
caption:
A new museum dedicated to the July Mass Uprising is opening its doors. Tickets are available online starting August 6.

The 'July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum' is set to open to the public on August 6 to preserve the history of the July uprising.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will formally inaugurate the museum on Wednesday, August 5, at 9:00 AM.

Culture Minister Nitai Rai Chowdhury and Information and Broadcasting Advisor Dr. Zahed Ur Rahman announced the details during a press conference at the Secretariat on Tuesday.

The inauguration ceremony will feature reminiscences from July fighters and members of the families of the martyrs.

A documentary film created about the July mass uprising will also be screened during the event.

Visitors can enter the museum by purchasing tickets online, with a limited number of visitors allowed per day.

Tickets are priced at 50 BDT for adults and 25 BDT for children.

Culture Minister Nitai Rai Chowdhury stated that action will be taken if specific allegations of corruption in the museum's construction are received.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
